public_identity_surface_label: Example State official voter-information site / organization identity policy
delivery_role_note: Site-name, organization, logo, favicon, and related identity signals help external systems recognize the official voter-information source, but they do not replace the substantive authority of the page or the direct office/help lane.
preferred_site_name_note: The preferred public site name matches the visible home-page identity and the responsible election office rather than a stale cycle label or unrelated government shell.
site_name_alternates_note: Any alternate names are bounded to real public variants of the same official source and do not introduce a different office or unofficial alias.
hostname_scope_note: The archive records which domain or subdomain is intended to carry the voter-information identity; subdirectory paths do not pretend to be independent site-name or favicon scopes.
canonical_homepage_policy_note: Home-page identity metadata points to the canonical home page of the supported domain or subdomain and remains consistent across duplicate home pages for the same site.
duplicate_homepage_consistency_note: HTTPS / www / non-www / emergency duplicate home pages keep materially consistent site-name and organization identity signals during migration windows.
organization_identity_note: Organization metadata identifies the responsible official office or government shell consistently enough that the public source is recognizable without blurring office responsibility.
contact_point_alignment_note: Contact metadata aligns with the current authoritative voter-help lane rather than routing users to stale or generic contacts that do not control election answers.
logo_and_favicon_policy_note: Representative logo and favicon assets help users recognize the current official source and are updated deliberately during rebrands, emergency replacements, or retirement of old election shells.
same_as_mapping_note: sameAs mappings are limited to the same organization on clearly attributable external platforms; they do not inflate authority with unofficial or stale identities.
subdomain_or_microsite_boundary_note: If voter information moves between a main government domain, election subdomain, or emergency microsite, the identity boundary and host scope remain explicit.
migration_or_rebrand_note: Identity transitions preserve a bounded trace of old and new names/hosts/icons/logos so stale recognition cues do not survive silently.
truthfulness_and_visible_content_note: Structured identity metadata remains representative of visible page content, current office responsibility, and current public help routes.
